title: Chemicals at the nose in the seconds when idling-scooter exhaust can be smelled (ESTIMATE / 推估)

conventions.central: P50 over 1,000 emission-and-share draws of ONE simulated red
conventions.low_high: (a) and (b): the signed flow factor F of the case combined with the grid factor 3 / 3 in log-quadrature is applied to the DILUTION before the smell test (corrections.md A1): low = P5 with the exhaust fraction / F_lo, high = P95 with the exhaust fraction x F_hi, so the flow uncertainty moves the share of smellable seconds and the levels never fall below the just-smellable level. (d): P5 / F and P95 x F (as final_numbers.py). (c) and (e) carry the emission and share spread only.
conventions.smellable: a second with odour units >= 1 (OU_hc10: exhaust fraction x D/T, HC-rich scooters x 10), D/T 800 and 6,800 kept apart
conventions.units: ppb by volume; ug/m3 at 25 C, 1 atm (ppb x M / 24.45); at 30 C every ug/m3 would be about 1.7 % lower (no verdict changes)
conventions.hazard: IARC groups in speciation.json are hazard labels only, not a risk from one red light; no cancer risk is computed; chemicals are not ranked by harm
conventions.comparisons: a seconds-long or red-mean value is never set beside a 30-min, 1-h, annual or lifetime value; only the converted averages (section d) are compared, and only with references of the same averaging time

simulationCautions: seconds within 1 m are grid-limited (about x0.3-3)
odour thresholds of raw exhaust from 1967-70 car-engine abstracts

threshold_level.what: level of each chemical when the exhaust is exactly at the smell threshold (1 odour unit), single idling scooter
threshold_level.method: raw-exhaust content / threshold dilution: 120 g/h / (F x D/T x w) x E_X / mdot x M_air / M_X; w = 10 for HC-rich scooters (signed OU_hc10)
threshold_level.note: a typical value at exactly 1 odour unit, not a minimum: an HC-rich scooter (odour x10) puts less benzene at 1 OU

xylenes.name: xylenes (sum)
flags: high end coupled with styrene high end (one Kumar peak)

butadiene.name: 1,3-butadiene
flags: high end from one rich start-up-plus-idle bike

styrene.name: styrene
flags: high end probably o-xylene; coupled with xylene high end

formaldehyde.name: formaldehyde
flags: high end car data or derived

acetaldehyde.name: acetaldehyde
flags: high end from one rich start-up-plus-idle bike

hcn.name: hydrogen cyanide
flags: no odour threshold in the researched files

notEstimated.name: benzo[a]pyrene (particle-bound)
notEstimated.why: Only car-derived per-km factors (EEA, motorcycle <250 cc rows built from car PAH factors) and a Taiwanese per-km BaP-equivalent with no matching THC; at idle lighter PAHs dominate and BaP forms mainly at 30 km/h (Chien and Huang 2010, abstract). No share of idle THC exists. It is particle-bound, has no smell and no short-term reference value.

notEstimated.name: phenol
notEstimated.why: Idle Nepal no-catalyst bikes give up to 5.4 % of hydrocarbons; EEA Euro 5/6 cars 0.01-0.05 %. The two disagree about 100 times, unresolved.

notEstimated.name: hydrogen sulphide
notEstimated.why: No measurement in scooter, motorcycle or car exhaust was readable.

notEstimated.name: sum of the 16 US-EPA PAHs; nitro- and oxy-PAHs; dioxins
notEstimated.why: No readable measurement with a matching THC; particle-phase traces.

notEstimated.name: sulphur compounds (OCS, DMS, SO2)
notEstimated.why: One idle test with negligible amounts (OCS 0.0014 %, DMS 0.0007 % of CO); SO2 below detection; no reference or hazard label researched. Not carried.

notEstimated.name: acetone, benzaldehyde, tolualdehydes, propionaldehyde, crotonaldehyde, butanal, butanone
notEstimated.why: Outside the question (no hazard labels or reference values were researched for them); several are car-only.

notEstimated.name: speciation of a modern fuel-injected, catalysed Taiwanese scooter at idle
notEstimated.why: No openable measurement (Dhital 2019 full text blocked). Whether a catalyst changes the SHARE of each chemical in the remaining THC is unknown; every share here is from carburetted or uncatalysed engines, or cars.

hazardLabels_IARC._note: hazard labels (strength of evidence that something CAN cause cancer), not a risk from one red light; not a ranking

confidence_rule: confidence of a chemical number = the lower of the case's confidence and the share's confidence
